Agent side (SRC): an org-wide agent registry already exists in the Application Plane (agentInstallationsForOrgForGateway, gateway GET /api/v1/agents/installations, ADR-0002, a presence-not-authority label surface) and the composer builds @-candidates from Space roster plus bound agents only, but nothing merges people and agents, and no agent-callable resolver returning ok/ambiguous/none exists in Model, Application or Control code (INF, from a negative grep of resolve_/lookup_/find_ patterns). The DM, group-room and guest targets the item names do not exist yet (Space kind is only personal/room/project/case), so a DM picker has no consumer today.

constraints: Plane ownership (SRC): people identity is auth-core/org-core (Auth Core is the sole membership authority); the cross-Space agent registry is owned by the Application Plane per ADR-0002, so a Control-owned combined directory conflicts with that ADR for the agent half. ADR-0002 says the registry answers presence, not authority: a resolver result must never imply the caller may invoke the agent, which still needs Control roster/decision for the specific Space. org-core members/search is service-authenticated with no per-user delegation and also returns invited emails, so it must be exposed only through the gateway with the session org and active-only filtering. Cross-org or external lookup needs the cross-org identity and privacy contract the UI research doc requires (SRC: VEREVON_UI_COWORK_RESEARCH_2026-08-13.md:128-132), so it must wait for F-t1-053. ZDR is not affected (names and emails only). The default ORG_MEMBERSHIP_LIMIT is 100 (SRC auth.ts:953-956), so client-side filtering of the existing list is enough at default scale.
approachAdjustment: Do not make Control the directory owner for agents. Slice 1 (S): add a search field to the existing add-member picker, or expose org-core members/search through a gateway route that forces the session org and returns active members only. Slice 2 (M): compose people (org-core/auth-core) and agents (Application registry) in the gateway, and expose the ok|ambiguous|none resolver as an agent tool through the gateway/capability path with presence-not-authority semantics. Defer external and guest lookup to the guest model.
effortNote: Unchanged overall, but the people-search slice is S because org-core search and the roster list already exist; the agent resolver tool is the M part.
verdictReason: Recommendation is valid but two premises are wrong: a people search already exists in org-core (just unexposed and with an invited-email leak), and the plane owner for the agent half is the Application Plane (ADR-0002), not Control. Also depends on DMs and guests that do not exist.

There is no guest principal (Control space_memberships only allows user or service subjects; Application room grants require an existing active org member and are hard-coded to role editor), no room-scoped invitation, no link or code invite with max uses, no approval queue and no stored terms acceptance. The product docs also state that external access needs its own cross-org identity and privacy contract before any invite list (SRC: VEREVON_UI_COWORK_RESEARCH_2026-08-13.md:128-132).
reuse: Better Auth invitation table and flow in auth-core (expiresAt already mandatory, status, inviterId; add a room target and a token for link invites)

constraints: Auth Core is the sole org-membership authority (SRC: org-core/internal/http/server.go:122-128 comment), so guest identity belongs in auth-core, not in Application. A guest must NOT become a plain org member (INF): org-visible documents and the organization-room roster sync would then include them. Room membership writes today flow Application spaceMemberGrants -> declarative PUT to Control, and ReplaceMemberships revokes any managed (user) member not in the declared list (SRC repository.go:744-775), so a Control-created guest membership of subject_type user would be revoked on the next sync unless the guest uses a distinct subject_type or the sync is scoped by source. Control space_memberships CHECK allows only user and service (SRC 017 migration line 62). Agent turns in a guest room must use the room recipient audience so retrieval is narrowed (ADR-0001); I did not trace that Data Plane honors the audience for org-visible documents. ZDR and residency apply to guest data. The org membership cap defaults to 100 and would count guests unless modelled separately. Link invites are a mass-exposure path: short TTL, max uses, admin revoke, rate limit.
approachAdjustment: Add a decision gate before building: choose the guest identity model (separate principal type versus restricted org role) and write the cross-org identity and privacy contract the UI research doc requires. Make one writer own room membership (see F-t1-054 source tagging) or give guests their own subject_type excluded from the Application declarative sync. Reuse the Better Auth invitation for the email path (expiry is already mandatory) and add the room target; ship link or code invites as a later slice. Keep guests out of the org-room sync and out of org-visible Data Plane documents.
effortNote: L to XL: no guest primitive exists in any plane, and the work spans an identity-model decision, auth-core, a Control membership schema and sync change, Data Plane visibility treatment, billing seats and agent-audience fencing.
verdictReason: Recommendation stays valid and the org-invitation base is correctly described, but the approach omits the identity-model gate and the declarative-sync clobber, and underestimates effort; keep it in the late wave.

exactGap: No usable team concept exists, but there is dormant scaffolding (SRC): auth-core defines team and team_member tables plus invitation.team_id in its Drizzle schema, the organization plugin config does not enable teams, and nothing reads those tables; resource_grants reserves a team subject_type in its CHECK constraint while the ACL repository rejects any non-user subject ("MVP is user-only"). Room membership has no source or provenance (space_memberships has only a free-text granted_by that the Application sync overwrites), and the only sync is a declarative full replace from Application, so team-derived memberships would be revoked as stale. There are no user-groups or group mentions in the gateway, Convex or the Space UI, and a grep found no Space-originated consumer in notification-core (INF), so group mentions have nothing to ride on.
reuse: auth-core team and team_member tables (enable the Better Auth teams option) as the team store

Control space_memberships plus ReplaceMemberships (add a source dimension)

constraints: Auth Core owns membership and org-core deliberately does not mount membership or policy mutations (SRC server.go:122-128), so the team store belongs in auth-core with expansion into space_memberships in user-core; the item names org-core and user-core. The membership writer must be decided first (INF from SRC repository.go:744-775 and spaceMembers.ts:243): Application declares only manual user grants with managed_subject_types [user], so any team-derived Control membership is deactivated on the next room sync unless the declaration carries it or the sync is scoped to source=manual. Team membership never widens an owner-plane ACL (ADR-0001). Notifications: Space mention delivery does not exist, so group mentions stay a later phase as the item says. Agents in a mentionable group must be opt-in because one broadcast can trigger many paid turns.
approachAdjustment: Start from the existing auth-core team and team_member tables instead of a new Control concept. Decide the single writer of room membership first: either carry a source per member in the Application declaration (manual or team:<id>) or let Control own writes with a source column on space_memberships and scope ReplaceMemberships to source=manual. Use the reserved team subject_type in resource_grants for team-level sharing.
effortNote: Unchanged: the dormant tables save a little, but the membership-writer decision and the sync change keep it L.
verdictReason: The gap is real, but the claim that no team concept exists is slightly wrong (dormant auth-core tables and a reserved grant subject exist) and the plane split should name auth-core for the team store and call out the sync clobber.

exactGap: audit-core already ingests JetStream events (session-core tool_action and tool_action_reserved, user-core erasure and dsar_export through a durable outbox, leads-core, conversation-core, ingestion) and serves GET /v1/audit and /v1/usage(/summary) with org, since, until, event and user_id filters (limit default 100, no cursor) plus a daily retention purge. The access concern is CONFIRMED by trace (SRC): the gateway list_audit only needs a session and forwards the filters, audit-core verifies that the signed delegation binds the org but never consults the delegated role, so any org member can read all org events including other users via user_id; the settings "Recent security events" panel is described as admin review material but is not gated. Missing: admin or auditor gating, cursor pagination, plane/subject/resource filters, export, Space decision and agent-invocation events (user-core decision issuance emits nothing and decisions are stateless signed tokens), and Space or agent dimensions on the usage ledger (cost-core Entry carries org, user, producer, run and model only).
reuse: audit-core store, API, durable subscriber and the daily runRetention loop
user-core durable audit outbox (gdpr_audit_outbox.go, subject prefix verevon.audit.v2.control.user-core.*, JetStream PubAck plus Nats-Msg-Id) for Space decision events

existing per-Space Activity route and conversation-core ListSpaceAuthorityEvents for the per-Space view

owner/admin gate pattern used by the org-core GDPR erasure routes (server.go:131-140)
constraints: audit-core enforces subject, plane and producer authority (subscriber.go:287-295), so each plane must emit its own events: Space decisions from user-core under verevon.audit.v2.control.user-core.*, agent invocations from session-core under verevon.audit.v2.model.session-core.*; Model-side subjects also need nats-provisioner manifest entries (SRC audit_publisher.rs:28-36). Metadata only: audit details JSONB must never hold message content or the decision token (ZDR); tool_action already carries data_category and zdr. Decisions are issued per effect, so persisting every decision is high volume (INF): record denials and effect-bound decisions with decision_ref, not every read decision. The admin role must come from the signed delegation claim (UserRole is already carried and verified but unused). A role-gated read path must not break the Trust Center tool_action aggregation, so keep a self-scoped member view. An export is a mass-exfiltration path and must itself be audited, bounded and token-scoped. Org retention for audit is a single global AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS; per-org values (org_compliance.audit_log_retention_days) are dormant (see F-t1-051).
approachAdjustment: Split out the access-control defect as an S security fix and ship it first: gateway requires admin or owner for org-wide reads, audit-core honors claims.UserRole and forces user_id to the caller for non-admins, and the settings panel is gated with the existing workspace-admin check. Then build cursor pagination, filters and the export token. For decisions, emit from user-core through its existing durable audit outbox, for denials and effect-bound decisions only. For agent invocations reuse session-core audit or run-lifecycle events. Add space_ref and agent_ref to cost-core usage entries through the producer, not by reading another plane database.
effortNote: M overall as written; the role-gating fix is S and should be tracked as its own W1 security item.
verdictReason: The suspected read-path defect is confirmed by trace and should lead the item; and "exporting signed decisions is cheap" is wrong because decisions are not recorded anywhere today, so emission must be built.

exactGap: Control signs retention_class, residency and deletion_scope into every Space decision (opaque required strings on space_effect_policies), but no plane has a time-based retention sweeper for rooms, threads, messages, agent memory or sandbox output: the only running sweeper is audit-core global AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS purge, agent_memory.expires_at is only filtered at read time, org-core org_compliance retention columns are dormant, and Session Core runs.retention_class is only zdr, persistent or zdr_waived. The deletion saga (Application coordinator, per-owner receipts with honest unknown/partial states, legal hold, adapters for Data, Ingestion and Model) is personal-Space only, and Session Core delete_space_threads is bound to exactly one owner_principal_id, so shared rooms (threads owned by each author) cannot be purged by it. Shared-Space deletion, owner approval and write fencing are absent.
reuse: Control space_effect_policies (with policy_revision) as the signed carrier for the retention value
Application spaceDeletionOwnerReceipts, reconciler and per-owner delivery adapters (Data, Ingestion, Model) for honest receipts
session-core delete_space_threads and the Letta semantic-memory receipt flow, generalized from one owner to all authors of a Space
audit-core runRetention loop as the sweeper pattern
agent_memory.expires_at and the review_state expired value
Control legal-hold records (space_legal_holds) which already outrank deletion
org-core org_compliance.data_retention_days: reuse or retire, but decide explicitly
constraints: ZDR must propagate (SRC retention_receipt.rs:1-30): a zdr run persists no content, so a TTL policy applies only to persistent and zdr_waived content and must never weaken ZDR. Control decides the policy and signs it; each owner plane purges its own data and returns an honest receipt, and Application may only request a purge, never delete another plane data (no cross-plane DB access). Legal hold outranks any sweep. ADR-0001 puts the Space lifecycle and deletion coordination in Application and the authority in Control. The existing owner adapters are request-bound to a deletion_request_id and an owner principal, so a scheduled retention purge needs a different authority class and service scope (INF). The item states that saga migrations 022, 023, 0026 and 0027 are not applied in staging; I did not verify that. Search and graph index purge and copies inside notification payloads stay open risks.
approachAdjustment: Phase it. (1) Add a numeric TTL to the Control effect policy (extend space_effect_policies rather than adding a new table) and build one sweeper in Session Core for threads and messages, which is the largest volume, plus the existing memory expiry. (2) Generalize owner adapters from "delete this owner Space" to "purge before ts for this Space" under a separate scheduled-purge scope. (3) Shared-Space deletion last, after owner approval and the write fence exist. Session Core purge must be re-keyed from (owner_principal_id, space_id) to space_id for shared rooms, since each author owns their threads.
effortNote: L to XL: six owner planes need new time-bounded purge contracts and a new authority class, Session Core purge is owner-bound and must be redesigned for shared rooms, and shared-Space deletion adds approval and write-fence work. Phase 1 alone is L.
verdictReason: Gap is accurate (policy label exists, no sweeper anywhere, saga personal-only), but the item hides how much of the saga is owner-bound; present it as phased work with the Session Core TTL sweeper first.

exactGap: Control resource_grants already supports role edit (DB CHECK, AclRepository normalizeRole, authz check returns view or edit) and reserves a team subject, so only the gateway shares.rs hard-coding of document, user and view (lines 111-115) and the document-only, view-only ShareDialog behind the ownership gate stand between the UI and an edit role; "document" is the only ownable type in resource_taxonomy.json, a space subject_type does not exist (CHECK allows user and team), and no access-request flow exists (negative grep). Blocking finding (SRC): user-core mounts POST/DELETE /authz/grant and GET /authz/grants behind requireVerifiedAuthzDelegation, which only admits GET /authz/visible and /authz/check with a v2 ZDR-bounded delegation, while the gateway signs v1 delegation for every user-core call, so the share write path is fenced off in Control today ("Disabled until verified delegation exists" in server.go). Documents already have a Space edge (documents.space_ref plus Control retrieval decision), which overlaps with a Space-subject grant for documents.
reuse: resource_grants and AclRepository (edit role, team subject slot, ListVisible and Check)
authz facade /visible and /check with the Data Plane v2 delegation clients

ShareDialog, ownership-gate honesty gate and the shared-with-me list
ADR-0001 intersection rule as the evaluation contract
constraints: ADR-0001: effective access is Space decision AND recipient audience AND owner-plane authorization, and Space membership never widens a resource ACL, so a Space-subject grant must only narrow or co-require, never add an independent path (SRC). Both resource_grants and space_memberships live in user-core, so the membership join is possible in-plane, but Space privacy, entitlement, ZDR and legal-hold conditions cannot be evaluated by a visible-ids query, so the owner plane needs a Control read-time decision as retrieval already does (INF). Every new resource type (canvas, file, artifact) must be classified in resource_taxonomy.json and its Rust mirror in retrieval-engine passes a parity lint, otherwise ValidateUserGrant rejects it. The access-request approve action must be human-only: grant a Control scope that no agent or Model service principal holds. General access conflicts with ZDR and residency, so default off per org. Agents (service principals) must never gain access through a Space subject grant. Grant administration requires the owning service to prove the actor administers the resource (SRC authz_facade.go:29-33 comment).
approachAdjustment: First unblock the write path: either add a verified resource-owner delegation (owner plane proves the actor administers the resource) or a dedicated gateway-to-Control grant-admin scope, because POST/DELETE /authz/grant and GET /authz/grants are currently rejected by requireVerifiedAuthzDelegation. Then expose the edit role (Control already supports it; only shares.rs:114-115 hard-codes view), add subject_type space with a CHECK migration, classify new resource types in the taxonomy with the Rust mirror, and build access requests on the activity inbox. For documents reuse documents.space_ref rather than duplicating it with Space-subject grants. Generalize the gateway routes to resource_type and resource_id only after the owner planes for canvas and files exist.
effortNote: M to L: the grant write surface is fenced off in Control and needs a new reviewed delegation mode, the taxonomy has a Go/Rust parity lint, and Space-subject evaluation needs a Control read-time decision. Drop the quick-win flag.
verdictReason: Premise "shares are view-only" is incomplete: the edit role already exists in Control and the real blocker is the disabled grant write surface; Space-as-subject partly duplicates documents.space_ref. Keep, but re-scope and raise effort.

exactGap: No visibility, directory, self-join or tenure rule exists (SRC): registered_spaces has no visibility column (privacy_revision is only a revision counter), space_memberships has no valid_from or join sequence, the gateway route table has no browse or join route, and the sidebar and listing show only Spaces in the caller Control index (a non-member already gets 404, so private-by-membership is today the only mode). Session Core applies only a recipient-audience-revision ceiling to shared-thread reads (rows newer than the reader decision are dropped), never a floor, so any current member reads the full history. membership_changed is published by user-core through JetStream fire-and-forget (errors only logged, no outbox) and consumed by session-core with a plain NATS subscribe by design, so a missed event is never replayed; the item text says "plain NATS" for the publisher, which is slightly off.
reuse: Control registered_spaces and space_authority_revisions (bump privacy_revision and membership_revision on visibility or join)
gateway control_space_index plus Application labels composition in list_personal_spaces (the directory can use the same intersect pattern)

session-core audience-ceiling filter on messages and threads (basis for a floor, see approach)
Control ReplaceMemberships and the Application intent record for the membership write
constraints: ADR-0001 (SRC): Application owns Space name, kind and lifecycle; Control owns membership, privacy decisions and revisions, so visibility belongs in Control and name or description in Application, and the directory must compose both in the gateway as the index already does. Membership writes today are an Application declarative full replace into Control (ReplaceMemberships deactivates managed users not declared, spaceMembers.ts:243), so a Control-native self-join would be revoked at the next sync of that room unless the self-join goes through the Application intent record or the sync is scoped by source (INF from SRC). Product intent is that team and external Spaces are visible only to explicit participants (SRC UI research doc), so org-public rooms are a deliberate Slack-style policy change: private by default and opt-in per org. Never widen an owner-plane ACL on join (ADR-0001). Room names in the directory must respect residency and ZDR. The tenure window needs a join marker: the existing per-message recipient_audience_revision stamp is a candidate floor (INF, low confidence, not traced through Application audience registration).
approachAdjustment: Correct the premise: membership_changed already goes out over JetStream; the non-durable part is the plain-subscribe consumer in session-core (by design) and the absence of a publisher outbox. For self-join, pick the membership writer first (Application intent record versus Control source-tagged writes) and keep rooms private by default with org-public opt-in. Default the history rule to full history for open rooms, which is today behaviour and costs nothing, and defer the strict tenure floor to the guest work (F-t1-053). Split the item: visibility, directory and join is M; tenure window and durable delivery are the L part.
effortNote: Unchanged at L, but recommend splitting; the visibility, directory and join slice alone is M once the membership writer is decided.
verdictReason: Absence confirmed and the feature is table stakes, but the approach must resolve who writes room membership (declarative Application sync would clobber a Control self-join) and fix the NATS description.

exactGap: The gateway already honors a client-supplied idempotency_key for Space thread create and append (spaces.rs required_or_generated at :136 and :192; the key is not in FORGED_SPACE_AUTHORITY_FIELDS) and Control binds it into the decision digest, but the composer never sends one and nothing dedupes (SRC): Control decisions are stateless signed tokens, and Session Core append_message_in_tx assigns a fresh ULID and derives the event idempotency hash from message id and sequence, not from the client key. The composer sends through the SSE POST /api/v1/chat/stream with one in-flight exchange (streaming, done, stopped, error), blocks while submitting and does not use the existing resumeStream/resume route that the main chat controller uses; the timeline is a 6 s poll with a latestThreadRequest ordering guard and a module-level published store (space-live-work.ts), and there is no offline versus service-down banner, only a threadsUnavailable flag. The unauthenticated static /health route exists in the gateway and is proxied by nginx, but it reports nothing about upstream planes.
reuse: gateway required_or_generated and the Control thread-append decision, which already accept and bind a client key and a content digest
chat-client resumeStream and the gateway /api/v1/chat/stream/resume/{request_id} route plus the use-chat-controller recovery logic
session-core events unique index on (org_id, idempotency_key) and derive_idempotency_hash
space-live-work.ts published store and the SpacePage latestThreadRequest guard as the minimal store and version guard
gateway /health (rate-limit exempt, nginx-proxied) as the reachability probe
constraints: Plane ownership (SRC/INF): the effective dedupe has to live in Session Core (Model Plane), not only in the Frontend Plane, because Control tokens are stateless and the gateway holds no dedupe state; the item lists Frontend Plane as sole owner. The events unique index is per org on idempotency_key, so a raw client key would collide across users and threads (INF): Session Core must namespace it, for example a hash of org, thread, author and key, and compare the content digest so the same key with different content is a conflict, not a silent return. A retried POST also starts a new agentic run, so dedupe must cover run start (or the client must reconnect through the existing resume route when it already holds a request id) or the second billed turn still happens. ZDR: the dedupe record may hold only the hashed key and content digest, never content. Space authority is unaffected because the decision still binds subject, Space and revision.
approachAdjustment: Re-scope into three slices. (1) Idempotency end to end (Model plus Frontend): the composer generates a key per send and reuses it on retry; Session Core derives a namespaced dedupe hash for append and run start, returning the existing message or request id; where the client already has a request id from the connected frame, reconnect with resumeStream instead of re-posting. (2) Connectivity banner (S): probe /health plus navigator online and visibilitychange events, shown with last-fresh time. (3) Descope the normalized store: keep the existing published store and ordering guard until server push lands (F-t1-003); coordinate send states and queueing with F-t1-032.
effortNote: Unchanged at M only if the store refactor is descoped; the Session Core dedupe is a Model Plane change and the main cost.
verdictReason: Core idea is right and cheap, but the dependency "verify Session Core dedupes" resolves negatively (it does not), the owning plane includes Model, and the normalized-store part is optional given existing guards.
